relevance.rationale: A genuine orphan, and a stalled-plan finding: docs/audits/2026-05-18-d2a-categorical-thimble-resolution.md L358-373 contains a fully DRAFTED ref() stanza for this exact document, complete with a 'Why' rationale reading 'spectral networks ARE the BPS/thimble decomposition for Seiberg-Witten theory; central charges are critical values; walls are d^2 S = 0 loci where two thimbles merge. This is the SW-period sister-theory of QOU's setup.' The stanza was never landed — grep -i gaiotto in references.ts returns only dimofte-gaiotto-gukov2013. The corpus target is real and specific: it has prop:mi-sw-abelianisation, prop:sw-period-residue-sum and prop:jet-sw-tau-decomposition (Seiberg-Witten differentials and periods on the colour spectral curve in T*P^1), and rem:thurston-relaxation explicitly says the residue sum becomes the Picard-Lefschetz thimble decomposition of the SW action. I read the abstract and the table of contents (§3 geometric description of BPS states, §5 the network at fixed theta, walls as trajectories, joints and wall-crossing). Verdict is supporting, not core: the folio consumes no specific theorem from it — it is the sister-theory context the audit itself identified, and the drafted 'Why' claims relevance, not consumption.

keyResults.statement: Spectral networks are networks of trajectories on a Riemann surface obeying local rules; they give a map between flat GL(K,C) connections on a surface and flat abelian connections on a branched cover, with walls as the loci where trajectories degenerate.
keyResults.useForFolio: The abelianisation statement is the published form of what prop:mi-sw-abelianisation asserts for the colour spectral curve; citing it gives that proposition an external template rather than leaving the abelianisation unsourced.

proposedActions.rationale: A ref() stanza for this document was drafted in the D2a thimble audit with a written rationale and never landed in references.ts; the SW/thimble blocks it was drafted for are still uncited.

Before citing, someone should check whether the abelianisation in this paper (flat GL(K,C) connection to flat abelian connection on a branched cover) is the same operation as prop:mi-sw-abelianisation's multiplicative-integral abelianisation on the exceptional divisor. They look analogous; I did not verify that the hypotheses match, so aid-proof is not warranted.
